No specific crash analyses were available for streets, defined by the Illuminating Engineering Society RP-8 (Illuminating Engineering Society, 2022) as roadways with pedestrian activities, and residential areas; in these cases, the guidelines are based on best practices and practitioner experience. Although fully adaptive lighting systems have the potential to achieve significant reductions in energy usage and cost savings, the implementation of these systems in street and residential areas has been slow. Many cities have considered street/residential adaptive lighting systems, including Richmond, Virginia, but only a few (e.g., Cambridge, Massachusetts, and San Jose, California) have actually implemented the capability. This slow uptake of adaptive lighting technology might result from the high costs of the luminaire controllers (over $100 per luminaire) or the potential for negative effects on traffic safety and resident security. To speed the implementation of adaptive lighting systems, enablers of the technology, in terms of hardware and cost, must be further investigated, along with its effects on safety and security. An analysis of the impact of adaptive lighting would allow the development of metrics to guide the design of adaptive lighting systems to ensure that changes to lighting systems will not negatively affect street users and residents. 1.1 Project Goals The goals of this project were to (1) investigate the applicability of adaptive lighting systems in street and residential areas and (2) provide guidance for the implementation of these systems to ensure that the safety and security benefits of the lighting system remain consistent for all roadway users, and the negative aspects are minimized. These goals will be accomplished through an investigation of lighting metrics that can be related to the performance (e.g., safety and security) of adaptive lighting systems in street and residential areas. 1 2 Literature Review In order to fully evaluate the potential impact of adaptive roadway lighting, a literature review was conducted to identify the relationships between lighting and safety and security, especially on low-speed streets and in residential areas, and to evaluate the impacts of implementing adaptive lighting technology for streets and residential areas on safety, security, comfort, and energy usage based on this relationship. This review considers all factors in street and residential areas that may be related to lighting and lighting design. This review informs the identification of metrics to be analyzed later during the project. Case studies of cities and towns that have implemented adaptive lighting systems are also considered. 2.1 Street Lighting Technology Street lighting provides a number of important benefits. First, it improves the quality of life by artificially extending the lighted hours so that activity can take place. Second, street lighting is the key to improved safety for drivers, riders, and pedestrians during nighttime by helping target detection on the road surface.
